Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 2884 of 2023
Petitioner :- Sunil Kumar

Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 2 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Satyendra Kumar Singh,Prince Kumar Srivastava

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Anjani Kumar Mishra,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.G.A. for the State.

The instant writ petition seeks quashing of the FIR dated 24.1.2023 giving rise to Case Crime No. 16 of 2023, under Section 3(1) U.P. Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act 1986, Police Station Lalpur Pandeypur, District Varanasi.

entities.text: U.P. Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The contention of counsel for the petitioner is that it is clear from perusal of the gang chart itself that in Column 6 thereof there is mention of Section 376 IPC and Section 3(2)(V) of the SC/ST but the same gang chart also admits that these provisions have not been invoked in the base case insofar Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147011079/
1 as the petitioner is concerned.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: These charges are against other co-accused in the gang chart.
On the strength of the above, it is contended that the gang chart has been approved by the approving authority in a mechanical manner without application of mind.
It lacks the subjective satisfaction which is necessarily required while approving the gang chart.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance upon a Division Bench judgement of this Court in Subhash; Gulab Singh; Anish vs. State of U.P, 1998 (1) JIC 405 specially paragraph 18 thereof.

entities.text: Anish vs. State of U.P, 1998 (1) JIC 405
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the paragraph 18 relied upon reads as follows:
"We are also to look to the records to see that prima facie satisfaction of the authorities was there that a person had "acted' before he is booked and proximite connection between the occurrence and the activity of the person sought to be apprehended."
The contention of learned AGA, on the other hand, is that it is true that Section 376 has not been invoked against the petitioner in the base case.
However, a charge-sheet has been filed against him in the said case crime number.

The format of gang chart is provided in Column-A and, from its perusal, it has to be said that it is the case crime number in which a person has been charge sheeted is required to be mentioned in Column 5.
There is no requirement of mentioning as to what sections are invoked specifically as against each individual named in the gang chart.
Therefore, the gang chart cannot be termed illegal in any manner as it complies with and conforms with the requirement of law, insofar as its preparation is concerned.
We have considered the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

We find merit in the submission of learned AGA that the Gang Chart prepared in the instant case is in the format provided in Form I appended to the U.P. Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986.

entities.text: U.P. Gangsters and Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Moreover, Rule 18 of the Rules states that "Gang Chart shall be sent only in the manner as given in Form No.-1 of these Rules."

On a comparison of the Gang Chart prepared in the case with the formant provided in Form No.-1,
we do not find any discrepancy.
The Gang Chart is definitely prepared in the formant specified under the Rules.
Moreover, the note at the bottom of the Gang Chart definitely discloses the correct status of the charges and sections invoked against the petitioner.
Therefore, there is no illegality in the manner the Gang Chart has been prepared.
For the same reason, we do not find any merit in the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner.

Since the Gang Chart has been properly prepared as per the Rules, the submissions of learned counsel for the petitioner have been repelled herein above and also because the allegations in the Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147011079/
2 FIR contain ingredients of cognizable offence, the FIR cannot be quashed.

entities.text: Sunil Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 2 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The writ petition, therefore, fails and is dismissed.
